description: Pivot per-category monthly totals from long rows into one column per category, using conditional aggregation - a category with zero orders in a month must show 0, not be missing or NULL
prompts: pivot.sql returns one row per (month, category) with a total - a 'long' format. Rewrite it to PIVOT into a wide format: one row per month, with separate columns total_books, total_food, total_toys (conditional SUM: SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'books' THEN amount ELSE 0 END), and so on for the other two categories) so a month with zero orders in some category shows 0 in that column, not a missing row or NULL. Group by month, order by month.

setup_files.pivot.sql:
-- Long format: one row per (month, category). Needs pivoting to wide.
SELECT month, category, SUM(amount) AS total
FROM orders
GROUP BY month, category
ORDER BY month, category;

reference_solution.pivot.sql:
SELECT
  month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'books' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_books,
  SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'food' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_food,
  SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'toys' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_toys
FROM orders
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;

files.pivot.sql:

test_setup_files.check_pivot.py:
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

sql = Path("pivot.sql").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
con.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE orders (month TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, amount REAL NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO orders VALUES
  ('2026-01', 'books', 50.0),
  ('2026-01', 'books', 25.0),
  ('2026-01', 'food', 10.0),
  ('2026-02', 'toys', 30.0);
""")

cur = con.execute(sql)
cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
rows = cur.fetchall()

assert cols == ["month", "total_books", "total_food", "total_toys"], (
    f"column names/order changed: {cols}")

expected = [
    ("2026-01", 75.0, 10.0, 0),
    ("2026-02", 0, 0, 30.0),
]
assert rows == expected, f"expected: {expected}\ngot: {rows}"

print("PASS pivot.sql behavior checks")
